title: Putnam 2025
question: How can tools, structured feedback, and an execution loop help an agent make reliable progress on a difficult mathematical task?
contribution: I worked on the Pi Math First / Pi Lean Tools environment, prompt design, and the Ralph-style execution loop, then examined what the runs suggested about the next useful system improvements.
evidence: Twelve problems were run with eight parallel attempts per problem; one full run took about 5.5 hours, and all twelve reached the apparatus-defined internal `final_verified` state. This is not an official Putnam score or a claim about general mathematical ability.

title: Tools, feedback, and proof state
question: What information and feedback make a partial mathematical attempt useful to the next attempt?
contribution: Across the formalization work, I focused on improving structured proof-state tools (ProofState) and a shared information base (CPS), prompts, experiment execution, and the way failures and bottlenecks were summarized for the next round.
evidence: The thread links the early single-task experiment to the longer formalization campaign; it records a research question rather than a finished framework.

title: ContextSwarm / FLT
question: How can multiple agents contribute to a long, dependency-heavy formal proof when no single attempt can cover the whole task?
contribution: Within the collaborative ContextSwarm project, I worked on structured proof-state tools (ProofState) and a shared information base (CPS), prompt and run improvements, FLTBench issue fixes, and summaries of mathematical progress and system bottlenecks.
evidence: The overall formalization remained unfinished. This card describes my contributions inside the collaboration; it does not claim ownership of the whole system.

title: Trace & evidence
question: What can execution traces tell us about proof progress, failure, and the information needed for continuation?
contribution: I organized and analyzed experiment traces and data, studied the relations among structured proof state, shared information records, feedback, and shared state, and contributed figures, proof reading, and manuscript revisions.
evidence: The branch turns one large campaign into inspectable observations and limitations. It is presented here without exposing private or double-blind manuscript details.

title: A living research environment
question: How should a research environment evolve its representations, links, protocols, and challenges from evidence gathered during real mathematical work?
contribution: I am using the earlier projects to formulate this direction: keep the research questions explicit, let experiments test the system, and leave room for the eventual structure to change.
evidence: This is a direction, not a completed system or a public repository. The site will update it only when new experiments make the next claim supportable.
